brand_interview.audience: Studio members booking on their phone between things
brand_interview.references: Feels like the studio: warm plaster, wood, black iron

brand.name: Harbor Pilates
brand.voice: A good instructor's voice: clear, kind, never loud.
brand.audience: Members booking from a phone between other things; new visitors deciding if this studio feels right.

accent.name: kiln
accent.rule: Punctuation only: the booked state, the active class, the one primary action per screen.

principles: Motion reveals schedule structure: rows settle into the week grid on first view
Confirmation is physical: a booked class card seats itself into place
Reduced motion collapses everything to opacity

sections.name: Schedule hero
sections.intent: A member lands and books in under ten seconds; a visitor feels the studio's calm
sections.layout: Full-width week strip above the fold, today centered, classes as cards on a 12-column grid
sections.content_notes: Real class names and times from day one. No stock photography; texture comes from the plaster ground and hairlines.
sections.signature_interaction: The week strip breathes: today's column is subtly lit, and scrolling the strip tilts cards a few degrees with inertia

sections.name: Class detail
sections.intent: Answer capacity, instructor, and level without a tap; book with one
sections.layout: Asymmetric 5/7: class facts left, booking card right, sticky on scroll
sections.content_notes: Spots left stated as a number, never a bar. Instructor name links to a one-paragraph bio.

sections.name: Booking confirmation
sections.intent: The moment of relief: booked, paid, in the calendar
sections.layout: Centered single column, receipt-like, generous whitespace
sections.content_notes: Calendar link, cancellation policy in one sentence, waitlist position when applicable.
sections.signature_interaction: The confirmation card seats itself: a 6px settle with a single kiln underline drawing beneath the class name

signature_moment.description: The living week strip: the schedule is the hero, today is lit, and the whole strip responds to touch with weighted inertia, so booking feels like moving something real.
